18/S0.subgoal: Introduce the lecture and explain the goal of discussing various tracking technologies in VR and AR.

18/S1.subgoal: Categorize the major types of tracking technologies used in VR and AR.

18/S2.subgoal: Describe the two types and components of electromechanical tracking devices.

18/S3.subgoal: Explain how electromagnetic trackers use magnetic fields to determine real-time position.

18/S4.subgoal: Describe the principles and requirements of acoustic or ultrasonic tracking.

18/S5.subgoal: Identify and categorize the three main types of optical sensors used in vision-based tracking.

18/S6.subgoal: Explain the operation and difference between outside-looking-in and inside-looking-out infrared tracking.

18/S7.subgoal: Classify and describe the three types of visible light tracking techniques.

18/S8.subgoal: Describe how fiducial tracking uses artificial landmarks to facilitate tracking.

18/S9.subgoal: Explain how natural feature tracking uses computer vision algorithms to estimate pose.

18/S10.subgoal: Describe model-based tracking using techniques like SLAM and PTAM.

18/S11.subgoal: Explain how 3D structure sensing is used to create 3D models for real-world augmentation.

18/S12.subgoal: Describe the function and characteristics of inertial sensors for tracking changes in motion.

18/S13.subgoal: Evaluate the use of GPS and enhancement technologies for positional tracking.

18/S14.subgoal: Identify and distinguish motion capture, eye-tracking, and hybrid tracking systems.

18/S15.subgoal: Summarize the core concepts covered in the lecture on tracking technologies.
